subject: Clarifications: tenant isolation, SCIM delta sync & SSO attribute mappings

From: Chris Walters <chris.walters@novagrid.com>

Date: 2027-12-01T09:02:00-05:00
Subject: RFP: follow-up on tenant segmentation, SCIM delta sync and SSO attributes

Dylan —

Thanks for the RFP package. Before we finalize the IAM section for the procurement committee, a few clarifications that will determine whether we can accept the standard terms:

- SCIM: do you support delta synchronization for Users and Groups (i.e., incremental change tokens / lastModified-based)? Can you provide approximate rate/throughput limits for SCIM patch operations and bulk imports?
- Tenant isolation: can we map multiple NovaGrid business units to separate logical tenants with independent admin domains (separate admin roles, audit trails, and billing tags)? Any cross-tenant admin delegation model?
- SSO: for our HR-to-app provisioning flow we need the ability to send custom attributes (employeeType, costCenter, managerId) and optional nested group claims to the ID token / assertions — can you confirm attribute mapping semantics and whether Redwood supports claim transformations (rename, conditional emit)?
- Evidence: if possible, attach any short capability matrix or export we can include in the RFP response.

We have a procurement window closing next Thursday (2027-12-09); if you can respond with short answers and a 30-minute technical sync early next week that would be ideal.

Regards,
Chris
Chris Walters
Sr. Procurement Manager — NovaGrid Energy

Chris —

Thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in our product security lead and our technical account manager to confirm the exact wording for the RFP. High-level answers up front:

- SCIM delta: Redwood supports incremental SCIM (change tokens + lastModified) for user and group updates; we also support bulk import endpoints for initial onboard.
- Tenant isolation: we support logical tenants with isolated admin domains and scoped RBAC; cross-tenant delegation is supported through explicit delegated-admin roles (audit logs per tenant).
- SSO attribute mapping: attribute mapping and claim transformations (rename, drop, static values) are supported; nested groups can be emitted as group claims or via a SCIM-based lookup.

I've attached a short SCIM capability matrix and a sample attribute mapping PDF. Can you give two time slots for a 30-min call next week?

Dylan / Marissa —

See answers below. I've kept each to a short paragraph you can paste into the RFP. Marked any conservative caveats as (note). Also attached the two files for NovaGrid plus a suggested short redlines document for procurement.

1) SCIM delta sync and bulk imports:
Redwood supports RFC 7644-compatible SCIM with delta sync via lastModified and optional change tokens for incremental consumers. For initial provisioning we offer a bulk import endpoint that accepts NDJSON/CSV and returns an asynchronous job id. Typical sustained SCIM patch rates on our hosted service are 50–200 PATCHs/sec depending on tenant size and plan; bulk imports are rate-limited and executed as background jobs (note: heavy initial imports should be scheduled during off-peak windows and may incur additional transient throttles).

2) Tenant segmentation & admin domains:
We provide logical tenant boundaries with isolated admin consoles, role-based access control per tenant, and tenant-scoped audit trails. Cross-tenant delegation is supported via explicit delegated-admin roles that can be granted limited read or manage privileges across a whitelist of target tenants (note: delegated admins are recorded in the target tenant audit log). Billing tags and usage attribution are available per-tenant.

3) SSO attribute mapping & claim transforms:
Redwood's SSO integration supports OIDC and SAML and provides a GUI + API for attribute mapping. Transformations supported include rename, concatenation, conditional emission based on attribute presence, and simple regex replacements. Nested groups can be emitted as a claim array or referenced via a group lookup endpoint; note that very large nested group payloads are discouraged for token size reasons and we recommend group-claim paging or group lookup patterns for enterprise-scale directories.

4) Recommended redlines / procurement language (summary):
- Include explicit rate limits for SCIM patch and bulk import operations and allow for scheduled off-peak bulk runs (we recommend an SLA exemption window for imports).
- Define a maximum token-claim size or agree on group-lookup vs inline-claims strategy to avoid assertion size issues.
- For delegated-admin workloads, require explicit audit retention and an agreed retention window for exported logs (we can provide export tooling).

Attachments included: scim_capability_matrix.xlsx, sso_attribute_map.pdf, redlines_proposed.docx

If you want, I can convert these paragraphs into the exact RFP text blocks and return by EOD.

Kimberly Park
